claim: Coolify's official minimum is 2 CPU cores, 2GB RAM, 30GB free disk; a real production server runs comfortably on 8GB RAM (~3.5GB used), 4 cores (20-30% usage), 150GB storage; installer sets up Docker Engine 24+ and /data/coolify.
quote: CPU: 2 cores ... RAM: 2 GB ... Storage: 30 GB free space ... production server runs comfortably with 8GB RAM (using ~3.5GB), 4 CPU cores (20-30% usage), and 150GB storage (~40GB used)

claim: The Coolify repo is coollabsio/coolify, Apache-2.0 licensed, with 56.6k GitHub stars, advertising 280+ one-click services and describing itself as a self-hostable alternative to Heroku/Netlify/Vercel managed via SSH.
quote: Repository: coollabsio/coolify ... Star Count: 56.6k stars ... License: Apache-2.0 ... 280+ one-click services ... open-source & self-hostable alternative to Heroku / Netlify / Vercel

claim: Self-hosted Coolify is free forever with full access to all features and no restrictions; Coolify Cloud is $5/month base (2 servers) plus $3/month per additional server, 20% off annual, where you bring your own servers.
quote: Self-Hosted ... Free Forever ... Full access to all features ... Cloud ... $5/month base price (covers 2 servers) + $3/month per additional server ... 20% discount option for annual ... bring your own servers

claim: Coolify offers four build packs to deploy from git repositories: Nixpacks (auto-detects language and generates a Dockerfile), Static, Dockerfile, and Docker Compose.
quote: Coolify offers Nixpacks, Static, Dockerfile, or Docker Compose build packs to create optimized Docker images ... Nixpacks checks your git repository and generates a Dockerfile ... can only be used on git-based deployments

claim: Coolify v4 reverse proxying runs through Traefik or Caddy from one dashboard with automatic Let's Encrypt SSL provisioning and renewal; v4 introduced multi-server support letting you add remote servers via SSH and deploy to any from the same dashboard.
quote: Reverse proxying runs through Traefik or Caddy ... Coolify automatically provisions and renews Let's Encrypt SSL certificates ... V4 introduced proper multi-server support ... add remote servers via SSH and deploy applications to any of them from the same dashboard

claim: Coolify v4.0.0 shipped April 27, 2026 after about two years in beta; as of March 2026 the project had over 52,200 GitHub stars and a reported 325,000+ users.
quote: Coolify v4.0.0 shipped on April 27, 2026 after about two years in beta. As of March 2026, Coolify has over 52,200 GitHub stars and a reported 325,000+ users

claim: Coolify itself consumes roughly 1GB of RAM before any apps are deployed, so the 2GB minimum leaves almost no headroom; 4GB is a realistic production minimum and 4 vCPU/8GB/100GB NVMe is the comfortable sweet spot for multi-app use.
quote: Coolify itself eats about 1 GB of RAM before you deploy anything, so the 2 GB minimum leaves almost no headroom ... 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / 100 GB NVMe is the comfortable sweet spot

claim: Coolify v4 is built on a Laravel/PHP stack run via Docker Compose with services including Postgres, Redis, and Soketi (WebSocket server on ports 6001-6002 in dev) for real-time status events.
quote: Soketi WebSocket server provides real-time updates with status change events for applications, services, databases, and proxies, running on ports 6001-6002 in development

claim: Coolify supports standalone one-click database instances including Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Clickhouse, KeyDB, and Dragonfly, and integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Gitea for git-based deploys.
quote: Coolify supports standalone database instances including Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Clickhouse, KeyDB, and Dragonfly
